Asos Sees Earnings Boost After Return to Growth
Asos said it expects full-year adjusted earnings at the upper half of its guidance range, after a key top-line metric returned to growth in its most recent fiscal quarter.

The U.K. online fashion retailer said gross merchandise value improved throughout the year through Aug. 31 and delivered growth in the low-single-digit percentage range in the final quarter of the year. The metric declined 5% for the year as a whole.

Asos said it expects to report a gross margin for fiscal 2026 of more than 50%, above its guidance range of 48% to 50%, leading to a jump of more than 25% in adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.
Full-year adjusted Ebitda is expected to be above the midpoint of the company's guidance range of 150 million to 180 million pounds ($198.6 million-$238.3 million), Asos said.
The company said it is making progress on a turnaround strategy, and plans to scale the moves that are generating results.
"The business is demonstrating consistent delivery, and importantly, our recovery is broadening despite the macro backdrop," Asos Chief Executive Jose Antonio Ramos Calamonte said.
